Value governance: Structured value; must not be set at category level on channels that forbid it.
Alternative names and synonyms: Served at; Available at; Breakfast only; Lunch; Dinner; Late night
Search and filter relevance: High; daypart filtering depends on this.
Safety considerations: Hours at item level only on delivery platforms; category-level hours are frequently disallowed.
Regional relevance: Global.

Definition: Coarse price band for filtering.
Permitted values: Currency plus enumerated bands; bands must be defined per currency and per market
Value governance: Enumerated bands defined by PEWA per market; businesses may add local bands but not redefine the standard ones.
Alternative names and synonyms: Price range; Budget; Mid-range; Premium; Price
Search and filter relevance: High for discovery.
Safety considerations: Bands must not imply value judgements about the business. Currency conversion must not drive the band.
Regional relevance: Global; currency differs across all five priority markets.

Definition: Whether the item is appropriate for a given meal occasion.
Permitted values: Breakfast; Brunch; Lunch; Dinner; Late night; Snack; Any
Value governance: Open multi-value list.
Alternative names and synonyms: Meal type; Suitable for; Good for; Daypart fit
Search and filter relevance: High; distinct from the availability window, which says when, not what for.
Safety considerations: None specific, but conflating this with availability causes items to disappear from menus that should contain them.
Regional relevance: Global; directly evidenced as a delivery platform attribute rather than a category.

Definition: How the item can be obtained.
Permitted values: Dine-in; Takeaway; Delivery; Room service; Buffet; Grab and go
Value governance: Closed list; menu-level values restrict item-level values.
Alternative names and synonyms: Dine in; Takeaway; To go; Delivery; Room service; Buffet; Grab & go
Search and filter relevance: High; drives which menus publish an item.
Safety considerations: None specific; the risk is a published item that cannot actually be ordered through the stated channel.
Regional relevance: Observed directly in published East African hotel amenity vocabularies.

Definition: Whether the item is a house speciality.
Permitted values: Yes; No
Value governance: Closed value list.
Alternative names and synonyms: Signature; Chef's special; House speciality; Chef's Special; Our speciality; Star dish
Search and filter relevance: Medium; supports discovery and cross-menu placement.
Safety considerations: Pure marketing state; must never be presented as an objective attribute.
Regional relevance: Observed in East African menus as a Chef's Special Menu and as repeated house-branded prefixes.

Definition: Whether the item is limited to a period or season.
Permitted values: Yes; No; plus a date range when Yes
Value governance: Closed value plus a structured date range.
Alternative names and synonyms: Seasonal; Seasonal special; Limited time; Today only; Seasonal menu; Chef's Special Menu
Search and filter relevance: Medium; contributes to availability discovery.
Safety considerations: None specific; requires a retirement date so stale items do not persist.
Regional relevance: Observed in Southern African and East African menus as an explicit seasonal section.

Definition: Nutrient values for the item.
Permitted values: Per 100 g and per serving where available
Value governance: Structured nutrient set aligned to the regional nutrition labelling standard.
Alternative names and synonyms: Nutrition; Nutrients; Calories; Energy; Macro
Search and filter relevance: Medium; increasingly a filter in health-oriented segments.
Safety considerations: Nutrition labelling obligations in the region attach to prepackaged food, not to served menu items; PEWA publishing values for served items is voluntary and must state the basis and portion.
Regional relevance: Regional nutrition labelling standards and the per-100 g basis are specified in the East African framework.

Definition: Declared sourcing or producer of ingredients.
Permitted values: Free text plus a claim state: Sourced locally; Imported; Unknown
Value governance: Free text with a state flag.
Alternative names and synonyms: Locally sourced; Farm to table; Locally grown; House-made; Made in house
Search and filter relevance: Low to medium.
Safety considerations: Regional food standards require that food is not described in a false or misleading manner, and EAC criteria require claims to be clear, accurate and based on scientific evidence. PEWA should not render unverifiable sourcing claims prominently.
Regional relevance: Global; 'house-made' is a strong differentiator in East African hotel menus.

Definition: Commercial performance class from popularity and profitability analysis.
Permitted values: Star; Plowhorse; Puzzle; Dog; Not analysed
Value governance: Closed list, computed not declared.
Alternative names and synonyms: Menu engineering; Star item; Plowhorse; Puzzle; Dog; Low performer; High margin
Search and filter relevance: None for customer discovery; analytic use only.
Safety considerations: None specific, but this attribute must never be rendered to customers and must never be used as a category.
Regional relevance: Global.

Definition: Relative popularity of an item.
Permitted values: Best seller; Popular; Staff favourite; New; Not marked
Value governance: Closed list plus optional numeric rank.
Alternative names and synonyms: Bestseller; Popular; Trending; Customer favourite; Chef's pick
Search and filter relevance: Medium for discovery.
Safety considerations: A declared or computed popularity signal can mislead if it is stale; PEWA should timestamp any computed value.
Regional relevance: Global.

Definition: The set of size variants of one item.
Permitted values: Reference to a variant group; variants carry their own name, price, weight and serves value
Value governance: Structural, not an attribute value.
Alternative names and synonyms: Half portion; Full portion; Large; Regular; Small; XXL; By the kilo; 2kg; (2kg)
Search and filter relevance: High; prevents near-duplicate items differing only by size.
Safety considerations: Observed menus sell plated and weight-based variants of the same dish side by side; collapsing them into one item would lose price and weight fidelity.
Regional relevance: Directly observed in Rwandan and West African menus.
